cards.text: God is still talking to Moses up on the mountain, laying out how to build Him a sanctuary so He can dwell among His people. He's already covered the ark, the table and the lampstand. Now He gets to the tabernacle itself: ten curtains of fine linen, with blue, purple and scarlet yarn.

cards.question: What does God say to skillfully work into those ten linen curtains?

cards.text: The ten curtains get joined into two sets of five, with fifty blue loops lined up along the edge of each set. Fifty loops, friend, lined up PERFECTLY, and I can't even get two sprinkles to sit straight.

cards.question: God says to hook the two linen sets together with fifty gold clasps. Why?

answers.text: So the tabernacle is one unit
So the light can shine through
So each set can stand alone

cards.text: Over the tabernacle goes a tent of goat hair, eleven curtains this time, one more than the linen. In the junk drawer, friend, the leftovers were ALL of us, so I'm very curious about this extra.

cards.question: The extra goat hair gets trimmed off so the tent fits neat and tidy.

cards.text: On top of the goat hair goes a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that, a covering of fine leather. That tent is wearing more layers than me, friend, and I've got an apron, a neckerchief AND a hat.

Then come the walls: acacia frames, twenty on each long side and eight at the back, every one standing on silver bases, braced with crossbars and overlaid with gold. I spent years in a junk drawer next to old instruction manuals, friend, and not ONE of them had silver bases.

cards.question: God says to set up the tabernacle according to the ___ shown to Moses on the mountain.

cards.text: Next comes a veil of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen, with cherubim worked into it. It hangs on gold hooks from four gold-covered posts standing on silver bases.

cards.question: What does God say to place behind that veil?
The veil splits the tabernacle into two rooms. The front one is the Holy Place. What is the room behind the veil?

cards.text: The mercy seat goes right on top of the ark, there in the Most Holy Place. Now the table and the lampstand need their spots.

cards.question: Where does God say to put the table and the lampstand?

answers.text: Outside the veil across from each other
Behind the veil on each side of the ark
Side by side next to the entrance

cards.text: Then a curtain for the entrance to the tent, embroidered with blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen. It hangs from five gold-covered posts with gold hooks.

cards.question: The five posts at the tent's entrance stand on silver bases, just like the wall frames.

cards.text: Next God lays out an altar of acacia wood, square, five cubits on each side and three cubits high. I stand on a gold base, friend, and I STILL couldn't see over that thing.

cards.question: God says to make a ___ on each of the altar's four corners, all one piece with it.

cards.text: The altar gets its tools too: pots for the ashes, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans. This altar comes with a whole tool set, friend, and I'm over here with one mustache.

cards.question: What are the altar and all its tools overlaid with or made of?

cards.text: A bronze mesh grate sits under the altar's ledge, halfway up, with a bronze ring at each corner. Then acacia poles overlaid with bronze slide into the rings, one on each of two sides.

cards.question: Why do those bronze-covered poles go through the altar's rings?

answers.text: So the altar can be carried
So the grate can be lifted out
So the altar can be tied down

cards.question: With a grate sitting halfway up inside it, the altar is built solid all the way through.

cards.text: Then God marks out a courtyard with walls of fine linen on posts, a hundred cubits on the north and south and fifty on the west. On the east side, toward the sunrise, fifteen cubits of curtain go on each end.

cards.question: On the courtyard's east side, between those two stretches of curtain, what fills the middle?
The curtain on the courtyard gate is plain linen with no colors worked into it.

cards.text: Every courtyard post gets silver hooks and bronze bases, and even the tent pegs are bronze. The TENT PEGS, friend, and I've never gotten instructions this detailed for ANY batch.
Then God tells Moses to command the Israelites to bring pure oil of pressed olives for the light.

cards.question: How long are the lamps supposed to keep burning with that oil?
In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil, who does God say will tend the lamps?

cards.text: Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and now he and his sons are on lamp duty. After years in a dark drawer, friend, a job all about keeping the light ON sounds wonderful to me.

cards.question: When do Aaron and his sons tend the lamps before the LORD?
God says tending the lamps is only for while Israel is out in the wilderness.

cards.text: That's the tent, the altar and the courtyard, all laid out. But God's not done talking to Moses up on that mountain, friend, so keep your apron on.

findings.problem: The whole passage is tabernacle, altar and courtyard building plans. The long-stretch rule names building plans 'like the tabernacle' as a stretch that gets one summary story card and no choice cards. The walkthrough instead gives two full stops of choice cards on construction details. Applying the rule strictly would leave one story card and no stop, which conflicts with 'A stretch never gets a stop of its own' and with choice cards equal to or more than story cards in every stop.
findings.question: When an entire passage is a long stretch, such as building plans, how should Prep handle it? Should it be one summary card, a short stop of choice cards on the key details (the veil separating the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, the ark's place, the lamps as a permanent statute), or something else?

findings.problem: The card states facts from outside the passage without references: God speaking to Moses on the mountain, building a sanctuary so He can dwell among His people (Exodus 25:8), and having already covered the ark, table and lampstand (Exodus 25). The card cites only Exodus 26:1.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The joke 'the leftovers were ALL of us, so I'm very curious about this extra' doesn't click right away. It's unclear what being a drawer 'leftover' has to do with an eleventh curtain, so a stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: No story card sets up Exodus 26:30, so the blank 'pattern' can only be guessed from wording the baker hasn't seen. The wrong answer 'tablets' also points to something Moses really did receive on the mountain (Exodus 24:12), so a baker could argue it fits.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The statement says the grate sits 'halfway up inside it.' Exodus 27:5 says only that the grate is set beneath the ledge so that the mesh comes halfway up the altar. Whether it is inside or outside is left open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Continually' is one word, while both wrong answers are three-word 'Only on…' phrases. The right answer stands out by its length and form.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'That's the tent, the altar and the courtyard, all laid out,' recaps the passage. The card also cites Exodus 27:21, but it tells nothing from that verse.
Multiple choice dominates both stops: 5 of 8 choice cards in stop 1 and 6 of 10 in stop 2. Each stop has only one fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
